title: Cardinal Alessandro Farnese to the nuncio Giovanni Poggio, Rome, 7 August 1542 (AAV Segr. Stato Spagna 1A, IA-1, ff. 64r-66r, DECODE R91)

documents.shelfmark: AAV Segr. Stato, Spagna 1A (IA-1), ff. 64r-66r (DECODE R91, ASV_i1025_SdS_Spain_IA-1)
documents.date: 7 Aug 1542 (the day is left blank on f. 66r, 'Da Roma alli .'; dated from the clear lines, which announce the peace legates named on 7 Aug 1542 and have Ferdinand leave Vienna 'alli 9 del passato' (9 July 1542) for the Nuremberg diet, and from Pastor V 472 n. 5, who cites Farnese to Poggio of 7 Aug 1542, Chigi L III 65, for the cipher's argument; catalogued earlier as Dec 1541 from DECODE's misreading '12bre' of 'et bene valete')
documents.route: Rome -> Giovanni Poggio, bishop of Tropea, nuncio with Charles V in Spain

plaintext.source: Not on the record or online. A readable text of this letter is in BAV Chigi L III 65 (Farnese's letters to Poggio): Pastor, Geschichte der Paepste V (1909) p. 472 n. 5, summarises its argument from there. Register copies of Farnese's letters to Poggio 1541-42 are in AAV Lettere di principi 14A, minutes in Naples, Archivio di Stato, Carte Farnesiane (Cardauns, NB I/7, 1912, pp. 435-439). None is digitised (DigiVatLib checked 6 Nov 2026); not seen.

transcription.source: DECODE transcription by MEG, 19 June 2020 (decode/DOC_R91_D2341_2341.txt, git-ignored; parsed to r91_cipher.txt and ciphertext_decode.txt); image re-read of every cipher line by the project with dots, struck digits and corrosion holes (reread/64r.txt, 64v.txt, 65r.txt), then a key-guided check of the unread stretches (KEYCHECK notes)
transcription.notes: 2,956 digits measured on DECODE's transcript (no dots recorded); the image re-read has 2,963 digit positions (digits the transcriber skipped at cancellations and holes added, struck digits dropped), 136 certain dots. Corrections counted: ~15 firm or probable digit corrections in the re-read plus 7 in the key-guided check; ~25 further alternatives marked '?'. Heavy bleed-through and iron-gall corrosion; holes at the right edge of 64r and the line ends of 65r; 64v.12-13 openings and 65r.15-18 illegible.

system.summary: Meister's key no. 2 (the Poggio cipher, Chigi M II 49): polyphonic single digits for vowels and consonant groups, two-digit syllable codes, dotted codes marked by a dot over the preceding digit, null 11.

diacritics.note: A dot over the digit before a code (sometimes over the code's own first digit) selects its dotted value: 80-83 ta te ti to, 84-86 qua que qui, 87-89 che chi non, 08 N.S., 00 S.M.ta; 83 of 136 certain dots stand before an 8.

system.doubled_letters: mostly written once (steso, efeto, tuto); bb has a code (02)
system.sibling_key: Same chancery and dossier as IA-2 (DECODE R92, Klee's key), which is a different design; Meister key no. 1 (Montepulciano) fails.
system.notes: Corrections to Meister's print found on this letter: b/c = 02 (Meister's 'or' a misprint), s/z/et = 1, null = 11, ci = 24, co = 26 (26 not in Meister); 23 undetermined. Polyphony: 2 = l/p, 4 = n/m, 6 = r/t, 1 = s/z/et, 01 = d/f/g, 02 = b/c/bb.

prior_solution.where: Key printed in A. Meister, Die Geheimschrift im Dienste der paepstlichen Kurie (1906) pp. 176-177 no. 2, 'Cifra ultima con Mons. Poggio mandata per il Montepulciano', never connected with this letter (Lasry-Megyesi-Kopal compared IA-1 with Meister's Poggio key without success, as cited by Klee 2026). No plaintext anywhere. Pastor (1909, V 472 n. 5) summarised the letter's argument (no open declaration against Francis I, who would leave the Church and seize its goods) from the readable copy in Chigi L III 65; found 6 Nov 2026, after the reading, and not used for it.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained the DECODE images and transcription (Sept 2026), set up Claude Code and posed the problem with the project's task template; the move to its own folder was the user's choice. No target-specific help.

solution.what: Web and literature search for a decipherment of R91 (Spagna 1A, Farnese, Poggio, Dec 1541) and Klee's article: none; Klee cites Lasry-Megyesi-Kopal's failed comparison with Meister's Poggio key.
DECODE transcript parsed (2,956 digits, 47 uncertain); full-size image checked: dots present that the transcript omits.
Digit and pair frequencies, doubled digits 0.88 of chance, pair IC equal at both phases (no fixed pairs), 9 mostly after 8 or 2 (not a free null).
Klee-style joint key and segmentation annealer (mixed one/two-digit monoalphabetic with null), built as the catalogue's first suggestion.
The annealer on a 2,956-digit stretch of IA-2 with Klee's key as truth: best -785.6 against -9 for the true key; not run on R91.
Meister 1906 key no. 1 (Montepulciano, 1539-42) applied as printed: no sense (-4.12 nats/char).

Meister 1906 key no. 2 (the Poggio cipher) applied polyphonically as printed: Italian at once (-2.19 nats/char): 'la qualita de la materia nondimeno perche', 'lo imperatore', 'Ingilterra et luterani', 'a la morte saluo la pace'.
Corrections by score gain: 11 = null (+867), s/z on 1 (+221); 11 = et rejected.
Greedy add/remove search over every value of every code: padded the text (nulls, then 'che', then 'e' on several digits); abandoned as a key learner.
potrebbe / sarebbe / farebbe -> 02 = b/bb; b/c on 02, Meister's 'or' a misprint (+246).
Image re-read of all 52 cipher lines by two agents: dots, struck digits, holes, ~15 digit corrections.
Dots: 83 of 136 certain dots precede an 8 (8 is 19% of digits), 9 precede a 0: the dot marks the following code as dotted, as Meister's 'con il punto sopra la precedente' says.
First reading passes with a token aligner: 64r-64v 0.681 certain, 65r 0.525.

All 24 orders of each syllable family scored: Meister's order holds for d, l, m, n, r, s; c-family ci = 24; then 26 = co found from ~15 readings (+262 nats; come = 2 6 0 6, l Turco = 2 6 0 6 2 6) and et on 1 (+113).
Scan of every unassigned pair seen 15+ times for a missing syllable: nothing above the padding level.
Second reading passes on key k2d with code-internal emendations: 64r-64v 0.689, 65r 0.627.

Key-guided image check of every unread stretch: 7 digit corrections where the glyph allows the predicted digit (beni de le chiese, di qualche concordia, the closing sentence, scriuete, esser de N.S. a tutti); candidates refused where it does not.
Merged reading aligned token by token (align91.py): 2,008/2,963 certain (0.678), 2,230 with uncertain words and 15 emendations (0.753).
Meister p. 177 page image checked: key no. 2 also prints Francia = 000 (beside N.S. ·08, S.M.ta ·00), missed in the first two passes; added to the aligner as a three-digit code.

Third reading pass with two new aids (probe.py: local decodes and crib fits; wordfit.py: dictionary lattice of 30,000 sixteenth-century forms) on every unread stretch, two parallel readers. New: 64v.8 'a l Francia nome', 64v.11 'la condenatione' (restoring an overwritten pair DECODE reads 2 2), 65r.8 'de Francia', 65r.9 'grose', 65r.6 'se[.]de'; nine sense-fit candidates refused because each needs a firm digit changed.
Merged reading re-aligned (align91.py): 2,025/2,965 certain (0.683), 2,261 with uncertain words and 15 emendations (0.763); 710 unread, every unread piece given a blocker.

Fourth pass: dictionary lattice allowing one miswritten digit per word (wordfit.py --slip), two parallel readers; a slip accepted only as a substitution between neighbouring codes or look-alike digits, with the clause then reading. 20 slips accepted (quanto, S.M.ta, di x2, considerandosi, nimico, facendosi sarebbe, apresso, interesse, li facultà; incarico, trauaglio, questo, dano, imperator, qualonche), seven candidates refused.

Code 23 tested: its 13 occurrences in read text all split as code + 3 (a); on the six unread runs no value (ci, ca, ce, co, cu, che, ti, ta, qua, gi) yields a non-padding word. 23 is not used in this letter. No digit group recurs across the unread runs (only 8048, three times), so no missing code word.
Merged reading re-aligned (align91.py): 1,998/2,965 certain (0.674), 2,362 with uncertain words and 35 one-digit emendations (0.797); 609 unread.

Cardauns, Nuntiaturberichte I/7 (1912) pp. 435-439, read for Farnese's letters to Poggio of Nov-Dec 1541: drafts in Naples Carte Farnesiane 707, register copies in AAV Lettere di principi 14A ff. 45-48, originals in Spagna 1A (2, 9, 23 Dec); the letter of 10 Dec 'nicht vorhanden'. None matches ff. 64-66 in content.
Close of f. 66r re-read on the image: 'a qui; et bene valete. Da Roma alli .' with the day left blank. DECODE's '12bre', the source of the 'Dec 1541' date, is a misreading of 'et bene valete'.

Clear lines dated: 64r announces 'questa deputatione de legati' to the Emperor and the Most Christian King to halt the war; 65v has Ferdinand leave Vienna 'alli 9 del passato' for the Nuremberg diet two days after starting the army toward Buda (army left 7-8 July 1542, Cardauns p. 219 n. 1), and Saxony and Hesse arming against Brunswick. Letter is of August 1542.

Pastor, Geschichte der Paepste V (1909) p. 472 and n. 5: Farnese to Poggio, 7 Aug 1542 (BAV Chigi L III 65) argues that an open declaration against Francis I would drive him from the Church to seize church goods, the cipher's argument; the peace legates Contarini and Sadoleto were named on 7 Aug 1542. Pastor app. 55 (19 Aug 1542, Chigi L III 65 f. 260) refers back to 'quanto le scrissi con el corriere'. Date set to 7 Aug 1542.

Clear copies sought online: BAV Chigi L III 65 and M II 49 not on DigiVatLib (IIIF 404, other Chigi MSS 200); AAV Lettere di principi 14A and ASNa Carte Farnesiane not digitised; Ehses, Concilium Tridentinum IV, search-only on HathiTrust (viewer would not render in Chrome).

texts.label: Farnese to Poggio, 7 Aug 1542
texts.summary: Farnese answers for Paul III the Emperor's demand that the Pope declare against France in the first weeks of the war of 1542: the Pope will do all his rank and honour allow and join against the Turk with all his forces, but branding the King of France the Turk's ally would need a condemnation he cannot give, would cost the Holy See the reputation it needs, and would push others to leave its obedience and seize church goods as England and the Lutherans did; hope rests on the two legates, and no remedy but peace.

reading_review.note: The read stretches build coherent Italian sentences across all three pages (the refusal to declare against France, the Turk, the legates, peace); after the fourth pass (one clerk's slip per word, 35 one-digit emendations in all, every slip word marked uncertain) holes remain in 64r.16-19, 64v.6-21 and the corroded 65r.15-18, so the reading is coherent but holed, normalised in reading_64_en.md and reading_65r_en.md.

outcome.notes: Read in part after four reading passes (the fourth allowing one clerk's slip per word); every remaining gap has a blocker (NOTES Remaining gaps). Written up 2026-11-06. DECODE queue entry under farnese1541.
